prosperous

/PROS-pur-us/ — stress on first syllable, rhymes with generous · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Prosperous describes someone or something that is successful and financially well-off.

The once-sleepy port grew into a prosperous trading city.

Worked Example

The kingdom's merchants filled the harbor with goods from across the sea, and the king watched his prosperous realm grow richer and more powerful each year.

Prosperous is more precise than just 'successful' or 'wealthy' alone. It combines financial well-being with ongoing flourishing and success—the realm isn't just rich, it's thriving across all measures.

Your Turn

Answer correctly to continue.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

successful: Successful means achieving the results you aimed for — a season, a launch, an exam can all be successful without anyone getting rich. Prosperous always includes money doing well: a prosperous family or town is succeeding and comfortably well-off at once.

thriving: Thriving means growing steadily stronger — a garden, a friendship, or a club can thrive with no money involved. Prosperous ties flourishing to finances: a prosperous business is not only expanding but earning well as it grows.

affluent: Affluent means having plenty of money, and it describes the comfortable life that money buys — an affluent neighborhood, an affluent family. Prosperous adds motion and success: things are being earned and going well, not merely owned.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

struggling: barely managing to get by financially

destitute: extremely poor, lacking even basic necessities

Where it sits · how well-off and flourishing someone is — modest → comfortable → wealthy → prosperous

modest vs. prosperous: Modest sits at the low end, far from prosperous: a modest income covers only the basics, while a prosperous one reflects flourishing, growing success.

comfortable vs. prosperous: Comfortable is weaker than prosperous: a comfortable family meets its needs with a little extra, while a prosperous one enjoys real wealth and expanding success.

wealthy vs. prosperous: Wealthy comes close to prosperous but is narrower: wealthy describes having lots of money, while prosperous adds ongoing, flourishing success — wealth that keeps growing.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — pro-

Prefix — pro-: for, according to (Latin)

Root — sper

Root — sper: hope (from spes, 'hope') (Latin)

Suffix — -ous

Suffix — -ous: full of, possessing (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: By the traditional account, prosperous is pro- ('according to') + spes ('hope') + -ous ('full of'): things going 'according to your hopes.' A prosperous town is one whose hopes have come true — successful and financially well-off.

Use the root in a new word: prosperity

Use the root in a new word: prosperity: The railroad brought decades of prosperity to the valley — prosperity is simply the noun form of prosperous, a time when things go according to hope.

Word Building

Word Choice

neutral / formal

Prosperous is a step up from 'successful' or 'wealthy' alone—it suggests a thriving state that combines financial security, success, and well-being. Reach for prosperous when you want to convey that something or someone is not just rich or achieving goals, but positively flourishing across the board. For simpler situations, 'successful' or 'wealthy' usually work fine.
